page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-4 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 31.0 GB of system memory. Operating with an allocation of 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance provides a high memory-to-core ratio within its family. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs allocated to the machine.

Storage on the c4d-highmem-4 instance relies entirely on external network-attached volumes, as no local physical storage is bundled. In addition, the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring cloud NAT or separately provisioned external IP addresses for public internet access. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the architecture permits applications with high memory footprints to run without paying for unneeded vCPUs.

Given its hardware specifications, the c4d-highmem-4 instance is structured for memory-intensive workloads that operate effectively on a modest core count. Common operational use cases include in-memory key-value caching layers, moderate-scale relational databases, data transformation pipelines, and enterprise application backends.

With its dedicated core execution model and substantial memory allocation relative to processing cores, c4d-highmem-4 offers balanced cost efficiency for tasks requiring considerable memory headroom without excessive vCPU provisioning. This profile fits memory-bound applications, including in-memory datastores, relational databases, data preprocessing jobs, and enterprise business services.
